summary:
All 53 CONTRACT §4 sprites are built procedurally in Blender (Cycles CPU, shared bl_common camera/lights at PPU 64, scale never changed) and packed into 4 trimmed Phaser JSON-hash atlases. assets/props/manifest.json lists all of them, and prop_check.py passes (exit 0).

The look is soft and toy-like: rounded bevels, saturated colours and warm wood. Snow is either real geometry (drippy caps on the pines, roof slabs that leave a coloured eave strip, small mounds on posts and lids) or comes from a shader that whitens up-facing surfaces. Rocks are slate grey with glowing orange ore nuggets. There are log cabins with lit windows, a red/cream striped food stall and a blue/cream merchant sled. The bread oven is a clay dome whose glowing mouth faces the camera. The smelter is a brick furnace with a crucible of molten metal. The mine entrance is a rock face with a timber portal, lantern, rails and an ore cart.

Stations have an idle frame plus a 4-frame work loop: embers, oven mouth, furnace door and smokehouse pit pulse by changing emission and light strength, and the saw blade turns 22.5° per frame, which loops seamlessly.

Items are chunky, have no shadow and lie flat in a 72x72 frame with anchor (36,54). Each has a stackStep between 8 and 14 px. The cooked fish is a grilled salmon steak with a seared golden rim, so a 20-high tower reads like the one in the reference image. All items stay readable at 32-48 px.

Props, stations, buildings and decor have a baked soft shadow falling screen down-right. It is tinted cool blue-violet, fades out at the frame borders, and the frames include extra margin for it.

fence_log_x and fence_log_y are 1 m segments of 3 logs about 0.9 m tall. Each is rendered with invisible neighbouring segments casting shadow, then the shadow is split between segments by a weight (a' = 1-(1-a)^w), so a run of segments tiles with no seams. I checked this by zooming into the preview.

docs/previews/props_scene.png is a mock village: sea, plaza, farm, mine, hunting camp, the fish tower and both fence runs. It also includes the real player and villager sprites from assets/characters (read-only), which confirms stations are about 2x character height. Total payload is 1.94 MB as full RGBA PNG against the 5 MB budget. Palette quantization is available but off by default, because Pillow's octree quantizer bands the soft shadows.
contract_gaps: Kinds chosen (the contract does not fix them): trees, stumps, rocks and crop_wheat_0..3 = 'prop'; bush_snow, snow_pile_a/b, ice_chunk, campfire, boat_small and all fences/decor = 'decor'; the five station_* = 'station'; market_counter, trade_post, worker_hut, chief_lodge, tent_a, upgrade_bench, fish_net, dock_pier, mine_entrance = 'building'. fish_net has no work anim.

Facing: iso-aligned buildings have their front on local -Y, which faces screen DOWN-LEFT. Two things face the camera instead: station_bakery's oven mouth and mine_entrance (rendered with yaw 45, manifest front 'S'). Mirroring a sprite with flipX also mirrors its baked shadow (it would fall down-left).
fish_net is a V-shaped trap: two net walls on poles meeting at the corner nearest the camera, open toward screen up (the sea). It is not a flat net lying on the ground.

item_fish_cooked is a grilled salmon steak (matches the reference tower), not a whole grilled fish. item_fish_raw is a whole blue-silver fish. item_ingot is steel (silver-blue), the logical product of the rusty-orange iron ore.
Atlases are full RGBA PNG; prop_pack.py --quantize exists but is off because it bands the soft shadows.
extra_keys: sprites[*].topPx: visual height above the anchor in px (for bubbles / progress rings)
sprites[*].footprintM: footprint in metres [a along X, b along Y] or {radius}
manifest.conventions: text explaining anchor / footprint / topPx / front / stackStep / shadows
docs/previews/props_stations_work.png (idle + 4 work frames for every station)
regenerate:
cd /home/user/nurient/frost-village && /tmp/bvenv/bin/python tools/blender/prop_render.py -- --force && python3 tools/blender/prop_pack.py && python3 tools/blender/prop_check.py
# Render only some keys or atlases (cached results are reused without --force):
#   /tmp/bvenv/bin/python tools/blender/prop_render.py -- station_grill crop_wheat_* props_items --force
# On the user's PC (Blender 4.2+):
#   blender -b -P tools/blender/prop_render.py -- [keys] [--force]
#   then: python prop_pack.py (any Python 3 with numpy + Pillow)
# Raw render cache: <tmp>/fv_cache/props, i.e. /tmp/fv_cache/props here. Override with --cache DIR on both scripts.
# A full re-render takes about 6-12 min on 4 shared cores.
notes_for_integrator:
FILES (all under /home/user/nurient/frost-village):
- assets/props/manifest.json
- assets/props/props_nature.{png,json}: 2028x360 sheet, 15 frames
- assets/props/props_buildings.{png,json}: 2016x1388 sheet, 36 frames (11 building/decor + 5 stations x 5 frames)
- assets/props/props_decor.{png,json}: 1376x336 sheet, 11 frames
- assets/props/props_items.{png,json}: 584x36 sheet, 11 frames
- Manifest atlas keys are props_nature, props_buildings, props_decor and props_items, with paths relative to assets/ (e.g. "props/props_items.png").

SPRITE ENTRIES
- Every sprite has frame name == key, plus atlas, anchor (normalised to the untrimmed frame), kind, frameSize, topPx and notes.
- Non-items also have footprint [w,h] in screen px: the bounding size of the ground diamond/ellipse, centred on the anchor.
- Stations also have anims.work = {frames: [<key>_work_0..3], fps, repeat: -1}. The frames are in the same atlas. fps: grill 8, sawmill 10, bakery 6, smelter 8, smokehouse 6.
- Items also have stackStep and icon: true. Draw copy i at y - i*stackStep. Values: fish_raw 11, fish_cooked 9, log 13, plank 8, wheat 11, bread 13, ore 12, ingot 9, meat_raw 11, meat_cooked 11, coin 8.

PLACEMENT CONVENTIONS
- World metres to screen px: +1 m along X = (+45.25, +22.63); +1 m along Y = (+45.25, -22.63). Depth-sort by anchor y.
- Fences: place segments 1 m apart along their axis and the shadows join seamlessly. Cap run ends with fence_post. The corner of an L-shaped fence looks fine with a fence_post.
- crop_wheat_* plots are 1.5 m and can sit edge to edge on a 1.5 m grid.
- campfire has no flames baked in. The game should put fx_fire about 20 px above its anchor.
- dock_pier runs along world +Y (screen up-right), 4.4 m long; its anchor is the centre and the land end is at -Y.
- boat_small's hull is cut at the waterline (z=0), so it suits the water texture.
- Baked shadows reach about 0.84 x object height toward screen down-right. Tall trees (3.2-3.9 m) and flag_pole cast long shadows.

STATIONS (input/output pad positions are not defined; the game decides)
- grill: long axis along X.
- sawmill: log on the left, planks on the right (+X).
- smelter: furnace door faces -Y; crucible on the +X side.
- smokehouse: meat rack in front (-Y).

BUILD NOTES
- Albedo compensation: the shared lights brighten side faces about 1.4x. prop_lib scales albedos by 0.8 in linear space (snow excepted) so rendered colours sit near the palette. bl_common.py and pack_utils.py are unmodified.
- prop_pack.py reads assets/characters/manifest.json read-only, only to place real character sprites in props_scene.png. It falls back to a capsule if that file is missing.

KNOWN ISSUES / LIMITS
- snow_pile_a/b are white and nearly invisible on pure snow ground. That is intended; they read on the plaza and dirt.
- The saw blade's rotation is subtle at 1x; the game's sawdust FX should carry the motion.
- tree_* footprint is only the trunk (r 0.42-0.45 m), so the canopy will overlap characters standing behind the tree. Normal y-sorting handles this.
- No git commands were run. The lead's earlier commit holds an older snapshot of these files, so they now show as modified.
